claim: The parametrization pass covers about 25 FlightPhysics structs.
why: Flight.jl lib/FlightPhysics/src (HEAD 67109d6f, outside W). The families the doc names count about 30 structs: Quaternion, RQuat, RMatrix, RAxAng, RVec, REuler (attitude.jl, quaternions.jl), Wrench, FrameTransform, MassProperties, KinData, AirData, eight geodesy value types (NVector, LatLon, Ellipsoidal, Orthometric, Geopotential, Altitude, Geographic, Geocentric), TerrainData, and about ten continuous *Y output structs. | The figure is an estimate, and about 30 is close enough to 'about 25'. The struct count at the design date (2026-07-12, Flight.jl 3945596b) was the same within one.

claim: Flight.jl's math already mostly writes `<:Real` or nothing in place of `::Float64` argument annotations.
why: Flight.jl lib/FlightPhysics/src: no function in the math takes a ::Float64 argument annotation. About 67 signature lines carry <:Real or ::Real, e.g. attitude.jl:61, 94, 114 and atmosphere.jl:322-329. The only Float64 annotations in signatures are return types (atmosphere.jl:103, 105, attitude.jl:94) and the throwing AbstractVector{Float64} fallbacks at aircraftbase.jl:286-287. | 'Mostly' undersells it. On argument annotations the code follows rule 1 almost fully.

claim: The `*` method in Flight.jl's attitude.jl is the live example of the third rule.
why: Flight.jl lib/FlightPhysics/src/attitude.jl:94: `function Base.:*(r_ab::RQuat, v_b_in::AbstractVector{<:Real})::SVector{3,Float64}` carries exactly the ::SomeType{Float64} return-type annotation that rule 3 (design/spec.md:3085) forbids. | The method is a live instance of the pattern the rule forbids, as the original wording had it (b4d8f5f7: 'see attitude.jl * for the live example pattern'). The current sentence can read as if the method obeys the rule. Clearer: 'is the live example of what the third rule forbids, a ::SomeType{Float64} return-type annotation on the continuous path.'

claim: The reimplemented `PIVector` gains a flag-gated reset face: `PIVector(; reset = true)` adds a `Bool` input face plus the event, and the default omits both.
why: PIVector is not in W. It belongs to the migrated aircraft library, and D-141 backs the plan (design/log.md:5303). The same shape ships in W's library: src/library.jl:956-965, Integrator(; x0, reset::Bool = false), with reset_ports at :450-451. Probe K8-050a: the plain form has u_types Float64 and no state events. Probe K8-050b: with reset = true it adds (reset = Bool) and the one StateEvent :reset. | No pending.md bullet owes a PIVector, and Redstone's PID (src/library.jl:2441) has no reset face. The claim concerns the future aircraft-library component, and nothing in W contradicts it.

claim: One fixed policy governs the face: a rising edge resets to the declared `x_init` values.
why: src/library.jl:964: the analogue's handler writes the declared init (x_init(c) = c.x0 at :958). The guard is the Bool itself under edge semantics (:454, comment :904-909). Probe K8-052a: a held reset fires once and then integrates (0.5 → 0.8 over 0.3 s). x_init is the declaration's real name (src/declare.jl:47). | D-141 spells it `init_x`. The companion's `x_init` matches the code.

claim: The reset implementation is internal, an ordinary guard/handler event.
why: src/library.jl:965: state_events(::Integrator{V, true}) = (reset = StateEvent(reset_guard, reset_handler),), an ordinary guard/handler event declared inside the component.

claim: The boundary-zero reset fires harmlessly because the regulator's declared inits are zero.
why: Flight.jl lib/FlightPhysics/src/control.jl:45 (Modeling.X(::PIVector{N}) = zeros(N)) and :86 (f_init! sets x .= 0), so a reset to the declared inits at boundary zero changes nothing. Probe K8-064b: a reset that is not holding does not fire at boundary zero.

claim: The engine's two PIVector instances are verified reset-free in today's code, where the saturation bounds and `int_halted` handle windup across unused phases.
why: Flight.jl lib/FlightPhysics/src/piston.jl:310-327: f_ode! runs frc and idle in every engine state. :424-447: f_step! makes mode transitions and calls f_step!(idle/frc), which is a no-op (control.jl:50 @no_step PIVector). Nothing writes their x outside f_init! (:295-307). Windup handling: control.jl:71-77 (clamp bounds, int_halted).

claim: The `RQuat` cast at use sites takes the explicit `normalization = false` keyword.
why: Flight.jl lib/FlightPhysics/src/attitude.jl:70-72: RQuat(v::AbstractVector{<:Real}; normalization::Bool = true). The keyword exists and defaults to true, so a cast free of invariants must pass normalization = false explicitly.

claim: The 4-wide rate is already what today's `Attitude.dt` delivers.
why: Flight.jl lib/FlightPhysics/src/attitude.jl:114: dt(r_ab::RQuat, ω) = 0.5 * (r_ab._u * FreeQuat(imag = ω)) returns a Quaternion, 4 wide (quaternions.jl:51 size (4,)). It is used as the q rate at kinematics.jl:219-220 and :310.

claim: Flight.jl's landing gear is never evaluated off-zero airborne (identically zero in the air).
why: Flight.jl lib/FlightPhysics/src/landinggear.jl:250-252: with no contact the Strut returns StrutY defaults. :403-409: Contact runs frc on a zero input and returns default ContactY (zero wrench). :467: f_step! resets frc while !wow, so the gear's output is identically zero in the air.

claim: The `norm`-at-zero guards are already in place in Flight.jl's C172 model.
why: Flight.jl guards: atmosphere.jl:330 (airflow angles below TAS_min_αβ), kinematics.jl:18-20 (χ, γ below v_min_χγ), attitude.jl:302-304, :339-345, :353-356 (norm_im > 0, μ > 0), landinggear.jl:420 (norm_v < 1e-3), propellers.jl:418-420 (ω floor). | Two sites are not guarded at zero: lib/FlightApps/src/c172/c172.jl:861 (Flight.jl's own trim cost divides by norm(v_eb_b)), and landinggear.jl:412 computes norm(v_ec_xy) before its guard and passes it on to get_μ. The first goes away with Flight.jl's trim. The claim holds as the audit's finding.

claim: A component's bundle key set is its contract's key set
why: src/declare.jl:855-874 bundle_names derives the bundle's fields from the declarations alone. x/s/m appear when the store declarations return a value, u when u_types is non-empty and y when y_types is non-empty. ws, t and Δt are added by fixed rules. src/executor.jl:117-143 builds NamedTuple{BN} from the BN type parameter. The nested u/y key sets are the u_types/y_types keys (gather over entry.inputs/entry.y). | Read as 'the bundle's key sets are fixed by the contract declarations', not as literal equality: the top-level keys are store letters plus u/y/ws/t/Δt. Under a bare contract (D-436) u or y is the value itself and has no key set.

claim: Every field-emitting component must expose (component, input values) -> handle as a plain, pure, public function
why: Redstone ships no field-emitting component: rg for field handles in src/ finds only a comment at src/leaves.jl:6, and src/library.jl defines none. The obligation falls on domain libraries, and nothing in W breaks it. | Vacuous at W: an author obligation with no shipped subject.

claim: The field-emitting component's swept output stage must be a one-line call to the value-level constructor, never the other way round
why: No field-emitting component in src/library.jl (struct list :42-1999), so W has no swept output stage that could put the query math the wrong way round. | Vacuous at W.

claim: The condition math of §14.1 can construct, outside any sweep, bit-for-bit the same handle the sweep produces from the same root-input values
why: This is the rationale for the value-level constructor. W ships no field handle (src/leaves.jl:6 is the only mention), so no code contradicts it. | Vacuous at W.

claim: The value-level constructor is a shipped component's obligation, not something a consumer can retrofit
why: An obligation on shipped field-emitting components. src/library.jl ships none, so nothing in W contradicts it. | Vacuous at W.

claim: For bulk-data components the obligation is only that the query math be reachable as a plain function
why: W has no bulk-data component (src/library.jl struct list), so nothing contradicts it. | Vacuous at W.

claim: Contract ports are log-exported
why: src/dataplane.jl:539-545: a Snapshot carries the whole store and layout, and the log keeps snapshots (src/dataplane.jl:657 log!). Probe P16 reads the declared port eng/P off every logged snapshot.

claim: Abstract container element types follow the same concreteness discipline as plain fields
why: Children are found by value for plain fields and container elements alike (src/assembly.jl:149, :153-157), with no concreteness check on either. Probe P11: a Tuple{AbstractComponent, AbstractComponent} container and an ::AbstractComponent field both build, giving kids/1, kids/2 and one.
